Private Sub HandleSlotPick(ByRef slotWb As Workbook, title As String, fileType As String, _
                           lblFile As MSForms.Label, lblStatus As MSForms.Label, _
                           ByRef validFlag As Boolean)
    Dim wb As Workbook

    ' (Workbooks.Open returns the already-open instance, so closing it would invalidate wb).
    If Not (slotWb Is wb) Then CloseSlotWorkbook slotWb

        lblStatus.ForeColor = RGB(0, 128, 0)

' (When the same file is chosen for two slots, Workbooks.Open hands back one shared instance;
' closing it for one slot would otherwise invalidate the other and crash on later access.)
Private Sub CloseSlotWorkbook(wbToClose As Workbook)
    If wbToClose Is Nothing Then Exit Sub
    Dim refs As Long
    If SelectedMain Is wbToClose Then refs = refs + 1
    If SelectedMissed Is wbToClose Then refs = refs + 1
    If SelectedEpic Is wbToClose Then refs = refs + 1
    If SelectedPrev Is wbToClose Then refs = refs + 1
    If refs <= 1 Then
        On Error Resume Next
        wbToClose.Close SaveChanges:=False
        On Error GoTo 0
    End If
End Sub

End Sub

usual designer-block format. Here's why and exactly what to produce.

You've been outputting .frm-style text like this:

    VERSION 5.00
    Begin VB.UserForm FilePickerForm
       Caption = "..."

          Caption = "Run"
          Height = 390
          ...
       End
       Begin MSForms.TextBox txtNewPath
          ...
       End
    End
    Attribute VB_Name = "FilePickerForm"
    ...

This format is ONLY valid inside a real .frm file created by VBE's File > Export,
and can only be loaded back via File > Import. It is NOT valid VBA source you can
paste into a code window. If someone pastes this into the VBE code pane, every
"Begin ..." line shows as a syntax error (highlighted red), and any control you
declared inside a Begin/End block (like cmdRun) does not actually exist on the
form -- so code referencing cmdRun.Enabled fails with "Variable not defined".

THE FIX: build every control at runtime in code, not in the designer.
Do NOT emit child control Begin/End blocks at all. Instead:

   controls), like this:

       ClientHeight    =   1500

    ' nothing needs to be drawn on the form by hand.
